subject: reasoning
question: A, B, C, D, Q, R and S are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. B sits third to the left of Q. R sits second to the left of S. Q is an immediate neighbour of both A and R. C is not an immediate neighbour of B. How many people sit between D and R, when counted from the right of D?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, Q, R and S are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table.

1) B sits third to the left of Q. 

2) R sits second to the left of S.

3) Q is an immediate neighbour of both A and R.

4) C is not an immediate neighbour of B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7de9333f12c0ce4b354d20e59476a85c43225c3c4fbbdab9106fa18fda90fc3b.png] 

Thus, There are **Two **people sit between D and R, when counted from the right of D

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
